summary: The DFW mid-cities industrial submarket remains tight, with Class B distribution product trading between roughly $105 and $122 per SF over the past 12 months and newer single-tenant buildings commanding a premium. Rear-load lease rates are holding near $7.25/SF NNN, and cap rates on stabilized deals have compressed into the high-5% to low-6% range. Owner-user demand from regional contractors continues to keep sub-$10M deals competitive, with well-located mid-bay buildings drawing multiple offers.
market_trend: Sale prices for mid-size DFW industrial have held roughly flat over the past year after a strong 2024 run-up.

price_discovery.note: Pricing has stabilized after the 2024 run-up, so buyers are underwriting to recent comps rather than chasing higher marks. A seller pushing materially above the comp range would likely need a standout building or a motivated buyer.

value_drivers: Mid-bay distribution space under 100,000 SF stays scarce in the mid-cities corridor
Two new spec projects near DFW Airport add supply pressure on larger boxes
Owner-user demand from regional contractors keeps sub-$10M deals competitive
